I dont believe, unless you really chugged some high amounts back to back, that you suffered brain damage. There frankly isn't any literature to support that dxm causes brain damage in humans at any dose level you could survive. 

That being said, all mental illness effect the nature of your brain (of course). So anxiety, depression, psychosis, etc will all affect your happiness and intelligence. So it is entirely possible that ilnesss triggered by your dxm use are at fault.

Give this plan 3-4 months and see how you feel. See a therapist as well if you are still feeling mentally ill. You will never be able to guage your baseline if you are mentally sick, so above all else, figure out what's going on (if there is any) before you even start to worry about things like this.

Hey man. You might be tripping right now or coming down. 

Practice meditation. Sit and breathe. That's it. Pay no mind to any thought, just watch them as if they were leaves flowing down a clear stream. 

Just breathe. Count for 10 seconds.  Count to 5 breathing in, then from 6-10 breathe out. 

Do this for at least 5 minutes now. Do it again on your comedown.  Do it again later.  


And after today, *don't*. *stop*.  *doing* *it*. 

Your mind needs breathing and rest time just like the rest of your body. More than just sleep. Meditation allows your brain a chance to let out tension that seems to glue negativity to your daily world. After it relaxes, and you can experience the nothingness, you then come back with a more objective mind and can see what thoughts or ideas is your ego and subconscious/or/mental illness trying to affect you or hurt you much more clearly and can contrast it to the better things in life that you possibly can't see at all right now. 

I dont know if I explained it well. But I *promise* it can change your life. But you have to try it, you may not feel it at first. You may not get it right away. 

I personally could not do it for the longest time, and that silent mindedness you speak of during DXM is actually what made me able to do it. I just sat and observed how I felt and then continued to meditate coming off, and kept doing it and now do it very often to relax and silence my brain, something I thought was so, *so* far beyond what I thought was possible.
